text: The opencode bundle mirror is hash-checked by nothing. src/bundle/manifest.json declares runtimes: [claude, codex] and holds 0 .opencode/ entries (.aof/aof.lock.json holds 37), and acd-bundle-manifest-hashes.test.mjs:23 re-renders with manifest.runtimes — so no control hashes the opencode mirror. It also hashes its own re-render rather than the disk, so a regenerated manifest beside a stale mirror is green. Raised at 124's refine; 124/02 closes it for its own three shatter mirrors only. The general hole is wider than that story.

aof work memory silently folds an unknown flag's value into the query. parseMemoryArgv (src/work/memory.mjs:190-192) skips an unknown flag without consuming the next argv element, so the value falls through to positionals and is joined into the query at :199. Measured: 'work memory recall "seam" --scope architecture --block' exits 0 and returns architecture-heavy records — the invented flag rewrote the question instead of erroring. Also: --block is real (parseMemoryArgv:163) but appears nowhere in 'aof work memory --help' (memoryUsage, :343-353). Out of 124/02's scope; raised at refine.
